Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis, which thrives in cool, wet weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown spots on leaves and fruits, premature leaf drop, and cracked fruit.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits.
Apply a recommended fungicide during the growing season.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation by removing fallen leaves.

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple leaf spots, black rotten fruits, and cankers on branches.
treatment: Remove mummified fruits from the tree.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Caused by the fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange leaf spots with tube-like structures on the underside.
treatment: Remove nearby infected cedar hosts if possible.
prevention: Avoid planting apples near cedar trees.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Leaves and fruits appear healthy and free from disease.
prevention: Inspect regularly for early disease detection.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green foliage with normal fruit development.
treatment: Apply fertilizer according to crop needs.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by the fungus Podosphaera clandestina.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, shoots, and young fruits.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Healthy foliage and normal fruit growth.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Caused by the fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long rectangular gray lesions on leaves that reduce photosynthesis.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Apply fungicides if infection is severe.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Exserohilum turcicum.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green leaves and vigorous plant growth.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Caused by the fungus Guignardia bidwellii.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots, black shriveled berries, and fruit rot.
treatment: Prune vines to improve air circulation.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: A complex fungal disease caused by several wood-decay fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-striped leaves, black spots on berries, and gradual vine decline.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Caused by the fungus Pseudocercospora vitis.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Brown irregular leaf spots with dark margins leading to premature defoliation.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green leaves and normal grape development.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Caused by the bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus and spread by the Asian citrus psyllid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Yellow shoots, blotchy mottled leaves, misshapen bitter fruits, and tree decline.
treatment: Control psyllid populations with approved insecticides.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Dark leaf spots, fruit lesions, cracking, and premature leaf drop.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Healthy foliage and normal fruit development.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas species under warm and humid conditions.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that become brown with yellow halos on leaves and fruits.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green leaves with vigorous growth.

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric rings on older leaves, leading to yellowing and premature defoliation.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris.
Apply recommended fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
Maintain proper irrigation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Practice crop rotation for at least two years.
Maintain proper plant spacing to improve airflow.

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions that rapidly enlarge, white fungal growth under leaves, and tuber rot.
treatment: Apply appropriate fungicides before severe infection.
prevention: Use resistant potato varieties whenever available.
Avoid overhead irrigation during humid weather.
Inspect fields frequently during rainy seasons.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green foliage with vigorous plant growth.
prevention: Keep the field free from weeds and debris.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy leaves, stems, and fruit development.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green foliage and normal pod development.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by fungal pathogens such as Podosphaera xanthii.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves, stems, and petioles causing yellowing and reduced yield.
prevention: Water at the soil level instead of overhead.
Grow resistant squash varieties when available.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Caused by the fungus Diplocarpon earlianum.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple spots that enlarge and give leaves a scorched appearance.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy leaves and normal fruit production.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas species under warm and humid conditions.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark leaf spots, fruit lesions, yellow halos, and defoliation.
treatment: Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown target-like lesions on older leaves, stem lesions, and fruit rot.
prevention: Mulch around plants to reduce soil splash.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked lesions on leaves, white fungal growth on the underside, stem blackening, and fruit rot.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and plants immediately.
Apply recommended fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
Avoid overhead irrigation during humid conditions.
prevention: Monitor crops frequently during cool and wet weather.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Caused by the fungus Passalora fulva (formerly Fulvia fulva).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with olive-green mold underneath.
treatment: Reduce humidity inside the growing area.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with gray centers and dark margins on older leaves.
treatment: Destroy infected crop residues after harvest.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Infestation by the two-spotted spider mite (Tetranychus urticae).
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny yellow speckles on leaves, fine webbing, leaf bronzing, and reduced plant vigor.
treatment: Spray plants with water to reduce mite populations.
Apply approved miticides if infestation is severe.
Introduce beneficial predatory mites where possible.
prevention: Maintain adequate irrigation to reduce plant stress.

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruits.
prevention: Remove infected plant debris after harvest.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Caused by Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) and transmitted primarily by whiteflies.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling leaves, yellowing, stunted growth, reduced flowering, and poor fruit production.
treatment: There is no cure for infected plants.
Control whiteflies using approved insecticides or sticky traps.
prevention: Grow resistant tomato varieties when available.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic light and dark green leaf patterns, leaf distortion, reduced fruit quality, and stunted growth.
treatment: Avoid handling healthy plants after infected ones.
prevention: Wash hands and tools before handling plants.
Control weeds that may harbor the virus.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Healthy green foliage with normal flowering and fruit development.
treatment: Maintain regular irrigation and crop monitoring.
